_comment: Notification-hook surface: every priority critical|high entry whose last_changed_at falls in the last 7 days, most recently changed first. last_changed_at = max(discovered_at, every non-internal updates[].at): it moves on a new finding AND on every reader-facing update, correction or improvement (updated_at moves only on a type:update record). Poll this file and alert on a new `id` OR a changed `last_changed_at` for a known id. `immediate_action` is non-null exactly when priority is critical. URLs are absolute (`url` == `permalink`; `markdown_url` is the entry's raw Markdown source). Schema: {id, url, permalink, markdown_url, priority, kind, headline, summary, discovered_at, updated_at|null, last_changed_at, updates[{at,type,summary}], immediate_action:{title,action}|null, actions[], exploited, kev, cve_ids[], cves[{id,cvss|null,status[],affected|null,fixed|null}], affected_products[], entities[], techniques[], tags[], sectors[], regions[], verification, classification|null, org_triage:{category,rationale}|null}. exploited = an exploitation tag or a CVE status of exploited/cisa-kev; kev = a CVE on the CISA KEV list. techniques[] carries the entry's MITRE ATT&CK ids (frontmatter + prose-derived, revoked ids resolved forward); classification is the collapsed Admiralty code (e.g. B2). For the do-now task list of every priority, poll data/actions.json. See docs/pipeline.md.

actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.
alerts.headline: Refrigeration attacks reach Switzerland, a Köniz butcher and three Volg stores; no actor established
alerts.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of French stores; on 2026-11-02 more than 115 stores in at least six more countries and the first German shops followed. The French blood service EFS confirmed on 2026-11-03 that an incident at its refrigeration supplier altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three EFS sites on 2 November, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, and ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action to mitigate exposure; no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers. SRF reported on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases in Switzerland, a butcher in Köniz whose freezer reached 50 to 70 degrees and three Volg stores whose cooling parameters were changed; BACS has received one reportable notification, and CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint warning on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers that names no vendor. CERT-FR reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited and Coop Switzerland says attempts against it failed, ANSSI says elementary flaws were exploited, controllers directly on the internet and weak passwords, and SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established. Reuters and Nextgov report that the Pentagon treats freezer failures at US military commissaries as a suspected hack. NCSC Switzerland's advisory, updated on 2026-11-06, says the public information does not establish a common attack method or confirm exploitation of the Danfoss CVEs it lists, and Ransom-ISAC's log of one Copeland XWEB Pro compromise shows 743 parameter writes in two administrator sessions, with default credentials claimed.

updates.summary: CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units. Blick reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores and sees no sign they were targeted.

Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

CERT-FR's alert has a third version dated 2026-10-16 whose guidance differs for compromised and uncompromised units: the whole configuration, defrost ranges included, is to be checked, and a compromised Danfoss unit is to be restarted or otherwise factory-reset and reconfigured, with a caution to check insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink. The Dixell France operator guide that the alert links says any XWEB PRO on firmware 1.12.1 or earlier must be updated without delay, that XWEB units ship with a factory Admin account, and that remote access must go through an encrypted VPN; neither document names an entry vector.

The Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links was replaced on 2026-10-18 and now carries Copeland's own bulletin of 14 October 2026, which acknowledges the vulnerability on a discontinued, end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers, says to remove every XWEB EVO from the public internet at once, gives a restore procedure and says to check product temperatures in the cabinets directly; the earlier statements about XWEB PRO firmware 1.12.1, a CISA advisory and a March 2024 bulletin are no longer on that page and are removed. Le Monde's report that the defrost operation was lengthened from one hour to eight so that alarms trigger late, and SecurityWeek's figure of about 700 supermarkets, the prosecutor's report of fires and the absence of a claim or ransom demand, are added, with Cybersecurity Dive's report that Copeland confirmed the flaw was found in discontinued controllers.

ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, not vulnerabilities researchers had published, so a firmware update alone does not close the exposure. Forescout, on 2026-10-22, counts 12,976 exposed service observations in 99 countries, 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1, and over 20 hacktivist-claimed refrigeration attacks since January 2026, and says the French access vector remains unconfirmed.

Reuters reports that the Pentagon treats late-August freezer failures at at least six US military commissaries as a suspected hack, with Cyber Command and Army investigators in touch with their French counterparts, and Nextgov adds that two people familiar with the matter say US officials suspect Iran-linked hackers; neither says how the intruders got in, and no official has attributed the activity on the record.

The attacks returned on 2026-11-02 across Belgium, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, Sweden, Ireland and Estonia, and Finland per The Guardian: BleepingComputer counts more than 115 stores and says it is unclear whether the attacks were coordinated, Sabcobel says its sites were hit through the same vulnerability as in France, Euronews names Danfoss as the software supplier in both incidents while CyberInsider says the manufacturer and access method of the new wave remain unknown, and Coop Switzerland says attempts against it failed.

The attacks reached Germany: heise reports an Edeka market in Reisbach whose cooling systems were heated to 50 degrees overnight into 2 November, WDR quotes a CAP supermarket manager saying the attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely and reports that Rewe's head office confirmed an attack aimed at Danfoss; SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established; and Le Canard enchaîné reports that cold rooms of a contractor of the French blood service were programmed to 110 degrees overnight on 1 to 2 November, with no source tying that case to these controllers.

The French blood service EFS confirmed that an incident at its refrigeration supplier on 2 November altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three of its sites, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, so the case no longer rests on Le Canard enchaîné alone; ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action, CSIRT Italia issued cold-chain measures, and no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers.

SRF reported on 2026-11-05 the first publicly known cases of the refrigeration attacks in Switzerland, a butcher in Köniz whose freezer reached 50 to 70 degrees and three Volg stores with changed cooling parameters; BACS has received one reportable notification about an attack on commercial refrigeration, and CISA, FBI, HHS, USDA and DOT published a joint fact sheet on refrigeration and cold-chain controllers that names no vendor, CVE or actor. No source names the controller make or the access route in the Swiss cases.

NCSC Switzerland updated its advisory on 2026-11-06 with the Swiss incidents, Copeland and Dixell XWEB and healthcare, a four-point checklist for refrigeration management systems across all relevant operations, supplier-managed equipment included, and the statement that the public information does not establish a common attack method or confirm exploitation of the Danfoss CVEs it lists. Ransom-ISAC published the event log of one internet-reachable Copeland XWEB Pro compromise (743 parameter writes in two administrator sessions, default credentials claimed without published evidence), and Unit 42 counts over 5,000 exposed devices across countries on 5 and 6 November and a falling count in France since October.

actions: On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run, deny web access to wp-content/upgrade/ in the web server configuration (not with an .htaccess file inside that folder) and confirm it answers 403 before installing 7.1.4 or the fixed release of its branch, because the update itself still unpacks with the old code and a firewall that WordPress itself loads does not run for that request; then confirm in Dashboard > Updates that each site is on 7.1.4 or the fixed release of its branch.

alerts.headline: CISA lists WordPress core's upgrade-window RCE race as exploited; block wp-content/upgrade before installing 7.1.4
alerts.summary: WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03; Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory. The discoverer says the update that installs the fix still unpacks with the old code, so the staging directory must be blocked before updating.

updates.summary: Wordfence assigned CVE-2026-119977 (CVSS 3.1 8.1) to the WordPress upgrade-window race after the entry was written; the statements that no CVE identifier exists are replaced and the CVE record is added.

CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03 on evidence of active exploitation, so the flaw is now listed as exploited; the catalog entry names no victim or method, and Wordfence's probing telemetry remains the only described activity.

The discoverer, Umut Bayram of Picus Security, shows that the update installing WordPress 7.1.4 still unpacks with the site's old code, so the staging folder under wp-content/upgrade can be reachable at a predictable path during that update, while a partial package exposes the installer only if it contains the installer files; he advises denying web access to the folder and confirming it answers 403 before updating.

alerts.headline: Cisco's mail gateway can be rooted by one crafted email; found in a TAC support case, exploitation confirmed

immediate_action.action: A remote, unauthenticated attacker gains root on the appliance by sending it one crafted email; there is no workaround and no mitigation short of upgrading. Cisco found this in a TAC support case, and CISA lists it as exploited. Upgrade every physical and virtual Secure Email Gateway appliance today and hunt mail_logs for the pattern Cisco names before assuming a device is clean; a clean result does not rule out the S/MIME injection.
immediate_action.title: Patch every Cisco Secure Email Gateway now: unauthenticated root RCE via a single email, already exploited

alerts.summary: Cisco disclosed CVE-2026-76461 (CVSS 9.8) on 2026-09-14: an unauthenticated attacker who sends a single crafted email containing SQL statements to a Cisco Secure Email Gateway can execute arbitrary OS commands as root. Cisco confirms active exploitation and says the flaw was found during the resolution of a TAC support case; there is no workaround. CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day. Cisco simultaneously shipped a hardening release fixing five further internally-found vulnerabilities in the same product; Cisco's hardening advisory says two vulnerabilities from its internal review are known to be exploited, this one and the arbitrary file write CVE-2026-76519. On 2026-10-31 Cisco re-released the 15.5.5-014 fix in light of new information related to exploit code available online, so a 15.5 appliance patched earlier needs a check of its Retro Remediation Engine version. Public Metasploit modules now exist for the exploited injection (merged 2026-11-05, its author's medium-confidence match to CVE-2026-76461) and for a second S/MIME injection that its author believes is CVE-2026-76443, for which Cisco names no fixed 16.0 build.

updates.summary: Cisco re-released the 15.5.5-014 fix on 2026-10-31 in light of new information related to exploit code available online, and advisory revision 1.2 of 2026-11-03 tells administrators of 15.5 appliances patched earlier to confirm with retroscannerstatus that the Retro Remediation Engine runs version 4.0.2 or later; 16.5.0-780 needs no such check. Cisco's hardening advisory, revised on 2026-10-14, also says two vulnerabilities from its internal review are known to be actively exploited, this SQL injection and the arbitrary file write CVE-2026-76519, and names no fixed 16.0 release for the hardening CVEs.

Rapid7's Metasploit framework now carries public modules for two unauthenticated SQL injections on Cisco Secure Email Gateway that end in root command execution: one merged on 2026-11-05 for the injection its author matches, at medium confidence, to the exploited CVE-2026-76461 and which needs URL Filtering and URL Retrospective Service enabled, and one for the non-default S/MIME public-key harvesting feature that Rapid7 believes is CVE-2026-76443. A clean mail_logs check does not rule out the S/MIME injection, and Cisco's hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 build.

alerts.headline: VulnCheck caught exploitation of the Node-RED flaw in Siemens IoT2050; all four variants affected, V4.3.4-1 fixes
alerts.summary: Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-834709 of 2026-08-11 discloses CVE-2026-58115, rated 10.0 on both CVSS 3.1 and 4.0: SIMATIC IoT2050 devices running Industrial OS with Node-RED installed do not enforce authentication on the Node-RED HTTP interface, so an unauthenticated attacker with network reach can create a flow and run code with maximum privileges. Siemens' advisory, revised on 2026-11-04, lists the Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants, all versions below V4.3.4-1; V4.3.4-1 is the fix, and Siemens offers uninstalling or hardening Node-RED as interim mitigations. VulnCheck reports that on 2026-10-30 one of its canaries caught exploitation, a single request that deployed a flow downloading and running a Linux bot, with web-shell flows from the same address since; the target was a canary and the activity looks like opportunistic mass scanning.

updates.summary: VulnCheck reports that on 2026-10-30 one of its canaries caught an attacker exploiting CVE-2026-58115 with a single unauthenticated request that deployed a flow downloading and running a Linux bot, with web-shell flows from the same address since; no Siemens device is reported compromised.

Siemens revised its advisory SSA-834709 to V1.1 on 2026-11-04 and now lists the SIMATIC IoT2050 Advanced, Basic, M.2 and SM variants as affected, all versions below V4.3.4-1 with Node-RED installed; the fix and interim mitigations are unchanged, so owners of the three further variants are in scope as well.

actions: In every Entra tenant you run or manage for others, list the app registrations that hold client secrets, starting with multitenant, delegated-admin (GDAP) and Partner Center apps, security-tool integration apps and Azure DevOps service connections, and search the service-principal and non-interactive sign-in logs for the invalid-secret or expired-secret errors AADSTS7000215 and AADSTS7000222 followed by a success for the same app; on any hit remove all client secrets, certificates and federated credentials on that app, including ones you did not add, disable its service principal if needed and rotate everything stored in any Key Vault it could read, because issued tokens stay valid until they expire.
alerts.headline: Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients, government among them
alerts.summary: Microsoft reports that since August threat actors have used the agentic framework ARTEX to query public GitHub for OAuth application secrets and cloud keys, and that from 2026-10-28 valid application credentials were used for service-principal sign-ins across dozens of applications in several tenants, a vendor-owned multitenant application among them. Todyl's telemetry shows one operator since 2026-11-01 targeting about 45 application registrations at MSPs, more than 33 of which authenticated, and reaching 27 organisations, government clients among them; Microsoft says a similar campaign involving the same addresses was reported by Todyl, while Todyl does not tie its case to ARTEX and cannot say where the secrets came from.

alerts.headline: Barracuda ESG: no login needed, watchTowr shows one request reaches root; update to 9.4.0.029 or later
alerts.summary: Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway (CVSS 9.3) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker restore a crafted backup archive through the configuration-import function, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection in the timezone field (8.6) that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway; chained, they give root. watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the chain needs no account, one unauthenticated request to the login handler reaching the restore function, and Barracuda changed its advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative interface must be reachable; watchTowr published a detection tool, and no source reports attacks. Barracuda names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the fixed build while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected.

updates.summary: watchTowr Labs published the full chain on 2026-11-05 and a detection tool: one unauthenticated request to the Email Security Gateway's login handler reaches the backup-restore function, a secret that is hard-coded in the product lets an attacker build a valid archive, and the restored timezone value reaches the root command injection, so exploitation needs no account; Barracuda changed its own advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606. No source reports attacks.

alerts.headline: Zyxel GS1900: Binarly says the exploit GreyNoise caught works on the June-fixed builds; install the .3C0 builds
alerts.summary: CISA lists CVE-2026-7273, a pre-auth stack overflow in the CGI of Zyxel GS1900 series switches patched in June in the .2C0 builds, after GreyNoise caught an actor it assesses is the same as or related to Red Heron exfiltrating configurations and hashed root credentials from 996 switches in 48 countries from about 17 August, 57% of them still on factory-default credentials. Binarly shows the recovered exploit works against all ten June-fixed builds because it targets a separate out-of-bounds write, CVE-2026-107441, which Zyxel fixed in the .3C0 builds on 2026-10-22 and disclosed on 2026-11-03; Binarly calls it an exploited zero-day on the strength of the exploit match and BleepingComputer repeats the label, while CISA's catalog lists CVE-2026-7273 and not the new flaw.

updates.summary: Binarly shows the exploit GreyNoise described works against all ten June-fixed GS1900 builds because it targets a separate flaw, CVE-2026-107441, which Zyxel fixed in the .3C0 builds on 2026-10-22 and disclosed on 2026-11-03; the .3C0 builds replace the .2C0 builds as the remedy, and exploitation of the new CVE rests on Binarly's exploit match, which neither Zyxel nor CISA confirms.

actions: In every Microsoft 365 tenant your organisation runs or administers, audit device code sign-ins with the authentication protocol filter of the sign-in logs and, where no documented device needs the flow, create a Conditional Access policy with the Authentication flows condition set to Device code flow and Block access, starting in report-only mode and excluding emergency-access accounts and, where devices register through it, the Device Registration Service.
alerts.headline: Vaud: device-code phishing against Microsoft 365 is running in Romandie; several organisations already affected
alerts.summary: The canton of Vaud said on 2026-11-04 that a Microsoft 365 device-code phishing campaign is running in French-speaking Switzerland and that several organisations are already affected: mail that appears to come from a company or a known contact leads the reader to type a code on a genuine Microsoft sign-in page, which gives the attacker access to the account. Microsoft documents a Conditional Access policy that blocks the device code flow for tenants that do not need it.

Update every Envoy proxy that has the Brotli decompressor configured to v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 or v1.36.12; the advisory names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable. On every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall on PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 or 11.2 that has TLS decryption enabled, run show system setting brotli and, where it returns Enabled: yes, run set system setting brotli-encoding disable until the hotfix for the release is installed; Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 lists every PAN-OS hotfix for this flaw as released.

alerts.headline: Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now
alerts.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available, and Splunk lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and lower among the products that include affected Node.js packages, with 10.2 or later as the upgrade target and its Visual Exporter app to be disabled.

updates.summary: Envoy and Microsoft have shipped fixes for the same Brotli decoder flaw: Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 lists v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 for deployments with the Brotli decompressor configured, and Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14) covers applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

NCSC Switzerland rates exploitation of the Brotli flaw unknown with a proof of concept available and names rejecting Content-Encoding: br as the interim measure; Palo Alto lists PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls that inspect Brotli traffic with TLS decryption enabled (hotfixes due by 2026-10-30), and PHP for Windows and Ubuntu shipped fixes. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26; JFrog shows the decoder reachable beyond HTTP and Cisco and Palo Alto report no malicious use against their products. The entry's earlier statement that no source reports exploitation is replaced, the priority moves from notable to high. Palo Alto's advisory, as read on 2026-10-28, shows six of its nine PAN-OS hotfixes released and three due on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30.

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0008.1 lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager as affected, critical (CVSS 3.1 9.8) on 9.1.1 and important (7.5) on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, with the patch pending and workarounds only; the SDDC Manager workaround is added to the actions. Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 records the last three PAN-OS hotfixes (11.2.4-h23, 12.1.4-h13 and 12.1.10-h3) as released, so the PAN-OS action no longer says they are due. Removed from the main text: ELLIO's reading of the attacker as a mass-exploitation operator and its count of 50 attempts (the 2026-10-28 section still carries them). The Ubuntu 20.04 entry in the CVE record now shows the ESM fix.

An earlier section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside the laboratory is dated to the day it held; NCSC Switzerland now rates the flaw actively exploited, and Zscaler's first-day decoy telemetry joins ELLIO's. Datadog's detection layers (decoder errors, worker crashes, leaked decompressed output) and what does not catch the attack are added, as is Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud Transporter Client.

Patchstack reports that default WordPress installs reach the Brotli decoder without authentication through the xmlrpc.php pingback and the operating system's libbrotli, shown to crash a worker but not to execute code; WordPress hosts need a patched libbrotli package, which the official WordPress image did not yet carry.

Splunk's advisory lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and lower, its Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA and Attack Analyzer as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them, with Splunk Enterprise 10.2 or higher as the upgrade target and the Visual Exporter app to be disabled, and Citrix names Unicon eLux Scout with hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR and 2605.1-3 as the fixes.

actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) or with the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, which says data of its insured persons and pensioners was stolen, that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with Pensionskasse Post, the Bernische Pensionskasse (which now says it must be assumed personal data left), the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT (which found data of about 1,800 of its insured persons on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more), a fund administered or advised by Libera AG or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope; also tell insured staff that cantonal police warn of investment-fraud calls from people who know their salary and pension details, which prove nothing about the caller.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment, project, test and migration copies included, and what it holds outside the productive system.
alerts.headline: PK Softech apparently kept Publica data it had promised in writing to delete; Tamedia says Akira holds about 100 GB
alerts.summary: PK Softech AG, the software supplier of Publica and other Swiss pension funds, says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT and that data must be assumed to have left; the Confederation headlined its 2026-10-08 release "data outflow confirmed", and the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Tamedia reports that PK Softech had confirmed in writing in January 2026 that it deleted Publica's 2019 migration data, which apparently stayed on its servers, and that Akira holds about 100 GB and demands ransom; Inside IT relays this and adds that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira took data, and Netzwoche relays that the authorities assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left. Publica says personal data of insured persons has presumably left; the Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich says its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Pensionskasse Post says personal data left, the Bernische Pensionskasse says it must be assumed so, the Ticino fund IPCT says data of about 1,800 of its insured persons sat on the attacked server and writes to all its insured because it cannot exclude more, and other funds are still checking. The Federal Data Protection Commissioner, who opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack; the demand rests on the press reports. The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich has suspended its planned 2027 move to PK Softech's system, PK Softech cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office has added the case to its criminal proceeding against Akira.

updates.summary: The supplier's customers are now named: the Bernische Pensionskasse (canton of Bern staff and three cantonal universities) says its supplier is the same company that serves Publica, the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse and Pensionskasse Post report the supplier incident, and Inside IT lists Migros-Pensionskasse and Syngenta Pensionskasse among the customers. None of the funds has confirmed which member data left.

Publica's own page of 2026-10-08 lists civil status and the IBAN among the data that could be affected and says its investigation indicates personal data of insured persons has presumably left. The AWP agency relays the software firm's position that it knows data left but not yet whether personal data is among it, that it may be business data, and that the volume is rather small.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, says on 2026-10-13 that it currently uses another provider, plans to move to PK Softech's system in early 2027 and is checking whether data from migration tests was affected. Publica's page says as of 2026-10-14 that it has no indications that data from the attack was published on the darkweb.

Cantonal police warn that criminals could use the leaked salary and pension data to phone insured persons with investment-fraud offers, SwissCybersecurity.net ties the warning to PK Softech, and the Zurich cantonal fund BVK says its PK Softech software runs in its own data centre so it is not directly affected; PK Softech can neither confirm nor rule out further affected customers, and the Ticino fund listed as a customer has made no statement.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich, the City of Zurich's pension fund, now says in its notice of 2026-10-15 that its inquiries indicate personal data of its insured persons and pensioners, handed to PK Softech as test data for a planned 2027 switch, was stolen, and that which fields were taken is still being clarified. Pensionskasse Post says in its notice of the same date that personal data did leave and no longer repeats its earlier anonymisation statement, though it is still unclear whether its insured persons' data is among it.

SonntagsBlick reports, from a confidential federal information note, that the Confederation rates the incident as serious and says the security organs of the Confederation are particularly affected, which it glosses as the Federal Intelligence Service, the Defence Group and fedpol, that the Federal Council was briefed on 2026-10-14 and that the cantons were informed; the Finance Department confirms only the briefing. NZZ adds that the pension consultancy Libera AG is also affected, that the Bernische Pensionskasse now says it must be assumed personal data left, and that Publica ran no regular on-site audits at the supplier.

Tamedia reports, and Inside IT relays, that the Akira ransomware group holds about 100 GB of the pension data of well over 100,000 current and former federal employees, with employer details of staff under cover identity among it, and demands ransom; neither the Confederation nor Publica confirms the actor or the demand.

Netzwoche, relaying Tages-Anzeiger, reports that the Federal Council and the security authorities now assume data on practically all current and former federal and federally affiliated staff left, federal judges and former Federal Council members among them, and that an on-site inspection at PK Softech on 2026-10-07 established the outflow of security-relevant data; neither the Confederation nor Publica has confirmed the actor, the demand or the scope.

The supplier's written pledge to delete Publica's 2019 migration data was apparently not kept, Inside IT relays that the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed Akira exfiltrated data, though that is second-hand and neither the Confederation nor Publica has itself named the actor, and the Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says all its insured could potentially be involved but has no evidence yet that data was taken.

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner (EDÖB) opened a formal investigation against PK Softech on 2026-10-22, after an informal inquiry at Publica on 2026-10-14, and states that data of several pension funds, Publica among them, was exfiltrated; the investigation is to establish which personal data the funds handed to the supplier, on what legal basis, and how much left.

The entry said that neither the Confederation nor Publica had named the actor. Publica's own newsletter of 2026-10-22 says the Akira group is being associated with the attack, and that Publica filed a criminal complaint with the Federal Prosecutor's Office on 2026-10-15; the summary, the sourcing note and the paragraph on the Akira reporting now say so, a population figure was trimmed from the analysis, and the demand and the Prosecutor's Office confirmation still rest on press reports.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich suspended its planned 2027 move to PK Softech's administration system; PK Softech, quoted by watson.ch, cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office has added the case to its criminal proceeding against the Akira group.

actions: Upgrade every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance to 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.6 now, internet-facing appliances first: the Canadian Cyber Centre lists every earlier build as affected, so appliances that took only the 2026-10-13 builds 25.1.1.2 or 22.8R2.5 are still short of the root-step patch; 22.7.x and below are not affected.

Run a compromise check on every appliance that was reachable on an affected build, starting with proxy, load balancer or WAF logs back to at least 2026-10-03 for welcome.cgi requests that carry an X-DSCGI-PATH header; where compromise cannot be excluded, first cut the appliance off from the internet and the internal network and snapshot a virtual appliance's file system and memory without powering it down, then follow Ivanti's recovery steps and reset the domain service account, LAPS and local passwords, certificates, API keys, the Kerberos tickets of its service accounts and the licence-server authentication the appliance held, because CERT-FR knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets.

alerts.headline: Ivanti Connect Secure chain: root step patched 29 Oct, CISA lists three flaws; 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5 fall short

immediate_action.action: Ivanti and CISA confirm exploitation of CVE-2026-104935, and Volexity saw the chain used against a fully patched 22.8R2.4 appliance from 2026-10-03. Upgrade every Connect Secure appliance to 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.6, internet-facing ones first: after Ivanti patched the root-escalation step on 2026-10-29 the Canadian Cyber Centre lists every earlier build as affected, 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5 included. Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool cannot see this chain, so an appliance that was reachable on an affected build needs a compromise check and rotation of the Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and other secrets it could reach.
immediate_action.title: Patch Ivanti Connect Secure now, then check the appliance and its AD account for compromise

alerts.summary: Ivanti disclosed the exploited Connect Secure authentication bypass CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13; Volexity saw it chained by UTA0576 with a root escalation, CVE-2026-111357, patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Ivanti patched the root step on 2026-10-29 and CISA listed it and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, on 2026-10-30; the Canadian Cyber Centre now lists every build before 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.6 as affected, which takes in 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5, the builds of 2026-10-13. A patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check, and CERT-FR says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance and tells owners to isolate and preserve it before any reset.

updates.summary: CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-14 says it knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets stored on the appliance, and sets the response order: isolate the appliance from the internet and the internal network, snapshot and keep it powered on, then analyse before any reset; its rotation scope also covers Kerberos tickets of the service accounts and licence-server authentication. CERT-FR also counts 25.1.3.0 as affected, so the fixed-build targets now name 25.1.3.1.

The unfixed root-escalation step of the chain now has its own identifier, CVE-2026-111357, published 2026-10-15, and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates it is exploited in the wild; its description names only 22.8R2.4 as affected, says the step was exploited in the wild in October 2026 and states no fixed build, so scanners, SIEM enrichment and tickets can now follow the step by ID.

The status of build 25.1.3.0 now rests on Ivanti's own description of the flaw, which covers versions before 25.1.3.0, beside Rapid7's table and CERT-FR's alert, which counts 25.1.3.0 as affected; 25.1.3.1 stays the target build.

Ivanti patched the root-escalation step of the exploited Connect Secure chain, CVE-2026-111357, on 2026-10-29, and CISA listed it and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, on 2026-10-30. The Canadian Cyber Centre and CISA now list builds 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5 as affected, so the builds of 2026-10-13 are no longer the target.

The Detection line again carries Volexity's on-appliance compromise checks (the temporary directory, network and memory forensics, the Integrity Checker's blind spot), and the binding of the first two chain steps to CVE-2026-104935 is now cited to Volexity, which states it.

Ivanti's own CVE record for CVE-2026-118527 (published 2026-11-03) now describes it as predictable filenames in Connect Secure before 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 that let a remote authenticated attacker upload files to a known location, and CERT-FR relays Ivanti's statement that all three chain flaws are actively exploited; the target builds and the compromise check are unchanged.

alerts.headline: C3RB3R ransomware encrypts Synology NAS; Synology confirms exploitation, 360 names the September 9.8 pair
alerts.summary: Synology said on 2026-10-29 that threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 to encrypt and extort devices on outdated DSM, naming no CVE and pointing to Synology-SA-24:20, while the Chinese vendor 360 identifies the ransomware as C3RB3R, a Cerber variant, and says it got in through CVE-2026-13684 and CVE-2026-13639, the two unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 flaws of Synology-SA-26:13 (fixed in DSM 7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 and 7.2.1-69057-12, with no mitigation). The two accounts conflict and no source reconciles them; a DSM that is current on both advisories is out of scope on either.

alerts.headline: VMware vCenter's pre-auth Syslog RCE is exploited; patch it with the auth bypass and VMXNET3 escape, no workaround
alerts.summary: Broadcom's VMSA-2026-0006 (2026-07-29) fixes five flaws across VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation and Fusion, and NCSC-CH, NCSC-NL and BSI CERT-Bund all carried it across 2026-07-28 and 2026-07-29. CVE-2026-59309 (CVSS 9.8) is an authentication bypass in vCenter's Directory Service reachable with nothing but network access to vCenter, and CVE-2026-59310 (CVSS 9.8) is a directory traversal in vCenter's Syslog server that reaches arbitrary code execution. CVE-2026-47876 (CVSS 9.3) is an out-of-bounds write in the VMXNET3 virtual network adapter that lets a guest administrator execute code on the ESX host, affecting only VMs using that adapter. No workaround exists for any of the five, so patching is the only control. All were reported privately to Broadcom, one of them through Pwn2Own, and CVE-2026-59310 has since been exploited in the wild and was added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-18; CISA also listed the ESX logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 as exploited on 2026-10-28, the day CrowdStrike said the actor WARP PANDA used it as a zero-day.

updates.summary: CVE-2026-59310, the CVSS 9.8 directory-traversal-to-code-execution flaw in the VMware vCenter Syslog server that Broadcom fixed in VMSA-2026-0006 and that this pipeline covered on 2026-07-30 as reported unexploited, is under active exploitation. German firm QUIRSO, working an incident-response engagement, identified 361 unique victim IP addresses across 47 countries whose first contact with attacker infrastructure came on 3 August (five days after public disclosure) with persistence established through a cron entry launching the open-source reverse_ssh tool for an outbound control channel. Switzerland's NCSC updated its VMSA-2026-0006 advisory to actively exploited on 12 August. No workaround exists; patching is the only remediation, and an unpatched internet-reachable vCenter now warrants a compromise assessment rather than an upgrade alone.

CISA added CVE-2026-59310 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-08-18. QUIRSO's continued investigation of the exploitation campaign this entry already tracks now reports a suspected China-nexus attribution and, in at least one case, deployment of Babuk-derived ransomware against ESXi hosts, but both findings trace to QUIRSO's own investigation alone; no independent assessor has corroborated either, and they are recorded here as QUIRSO's assessment rather than established fact.

The summary still said none of the five flaws was reported exploited; CVE-2026-59310 has been exploited in the wild since before the 2026-08-13 update and was added to CISA's KEV catalog on 2026-08-18. The Hacker News quotation, in the evidence and in the 2026-08-17 analysis, now carries the article's own sentence instead of a bracketed insertion. A duplicated vCenter patch action is folded into the one that also carries the compromise check. The sourcing note dates its no-exploitation statement to first publication. The analysis sentence on out-of-cycle handling is dated the same way. QUIRSO's single-appliance finding of activity consistent with exploitation of CVE-2026-59309, reported on 2026-08-17 and missing from the entry, is added and attributed. The 2026-08-28 attribution clause now cites The Hacker News, which carries it, ahead of the Infosecurity Magazine quotation.

CISA added the ESX insufficient-logging flaw CVE-2026-41709 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28, and CrowdStrike says the actor WARP PANDA exploited it as a zero-day in vCenter-environment intrusions as late as early 2026; Broadcom's advisory still carries no exploitation statement. The CVE record moves to exploited and KEV-listed, and ESX audit logs can no longer be treated as a complete record of administrator activity.

Broadcom's revisions of 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-19 (the 8.0 U2f express patches and the 7.0 extended-support path) are now in the fixed builds and actions; the Infosecurity Magazine attribution and date are corrected, CISA's ransomware-use flag on CVE-2026-59310 is recorded, the network attack vector of the two lower-severity flaws and the researcher credit are fixed, and the headline is current.

alerts.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php, with no upstream release for PHP 8.1 and older and a third path, CVE-2026-115560, left unfixed (keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0). CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, after a honeypot operator documented 35 successful code executions on PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker mod_php and VulnCheck extended its working exploit across builds of PHP 8.2 to 8.5; GreyNoise's sensors have recorded shell sessions since 2026-10-28, Palo Alto Networks' advisory now reports active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, Dream Research recovered a custom build chained with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that rooted 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and attacked a US government-affiliated network, SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the flaws without naming a CVE, and Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to them. As of 2026-10-22 BACS knew of no attack in Switzerland but said federal PHP applications were affected and that it had no complete overview of the update status, and Swiss cantons, universities, Cyon, the Lodur platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.

updates.summary: The fixed releases (PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35) shipped on 2026-10-21, so the earlier no-fix status ends; Cloudflare, watchTowr and VulnCheck report attack traffic and at least one unsuccessful web-shell attempt, proofs of concept are circulating, VulnCheck holds an exploit that succeeds with ASLR enabled and no source reports a confirmed compromise, so priority moves to critical. Swiss cantons, universities, the Lodur fire-brigade platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution, and BACS, CERT-EU and ENISA tell operators to update the runtime, check embedded installations and look for compromise.

BACS says it knows of no attack in Switzerland but that PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; the host Cyon took more than 100,000 sites offline for hours, a UK minister reports 32 government services unavailable with no confirmed compromise, and AWS reports a first exploit attempt on 2026-10-17. Sansec and Red Hat judge exploitation harder than VulnCheck's exploit suggests, and Palo Alto now schedules PAN-OS hotfixes for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.

Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation; PHP adds an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix, and advises session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until its next regular release. VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26, and Cisco, Splunk and Palo Alto Networks revised their product statuses.

Tenable's patch SC-202610.2 updates the PHP bundled in Security Center and Enclave Security to 8.2.35, and Siemens lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices running PAN-OS as affected with patch information only through customer support. ReliaQuest's lab reproduction gives a log sequence for detection (a POST returning HTTP 500, PHP memory exhaustion in Unknown on line 0, heap corruption, an Apache worker abort within seconds) and it has not seen successful exploitation in customer environments.

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws and says it cannot confirm that the initial access is associated with them; the summary, the detection guidance and the 2026-10-24 section no longer carry that account. Priority stays critical: the scanning, attack attempts, public proofs of concept and VulnCheck's working exploit do not rest on the retracted report, and no source ties a confirmed compromise to these flaws.

CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 after a honeypot operator documented the first successful code execution (35 shells on three PHP 8.4.26 mod_php targets); no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise. VulnCheck's exploit now also covers PHP 8.2 and 8.3 builds on mod_php, and SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the PHP flaw; the entry's earlier statements that neither flaw was listed and that no source reported successful exploitation are replaced.

Palo Alto Networks' advisory for both flaws now says that active exploitation has been observed against its PAN-OS management interface exposed to the internet, after a copy of 2026-10-27 said very limited exploitation; it names no victim or actor, and Unit 42's retraction of 2026-10-25 stands. Priority stays critical.

Dream Research reports a production chain of a custom PHP2Shell build with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that gave unauthenticated root on 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and led to an attack on the Active Directory of a US government-affiliated organization; CISA's catalog entry for the kernel flaw of 2026-10-28 says the same chaining. The earlier statement that no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise is replaced, an action for appliances that embed PHP is added, the URWB fix date in the vendor list is corrected from March 2027 to November 2026 (advisory version 1.9), and the PAN-OS hotfix status is updated to nineteen of twenty released (advisory of 2026-10-29). Removed from the text: the sentence on the release time, Karimi's two-source-address-clusters and PHPSESSID remarks in the main text (the 2026-10-27 section keeps his reliability caveat), VulnCheck's failed web-shell attempt in the main text (the Detection line keeps it), the lab log-path remark and most of Sansec's note on its CVE attribution (kept as a short clause); the 'no source ties a named CVE' statement of 2026-10-27 is dated, and the evidence record for Karimi's clusters remark is dropped.

GreyNoise's live tracker records successful exploitation on its deliberately vulnerable sensors from 2026-10-28, with reverse shells, a .ssh directory under /var/www, cloud-metadata queries and secret-scanning tools in the sessions of 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-31; Hunt.io reports that an operator's attempt against a national government failed because session files lay outside the webroot, and relays that PAN-OS firewalls were rooted in production. Dream Research's updated report names Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS as the product behind the chain first described with an unnamed vendor, which Unit 42 says it verified.

Morphisec reports PHP2Shell post-exploitation on a Windows server running IIS with PHP-CGI (the IIS worker starting php-cgi.exe, a command shell and a packed reverse-shell payload), the first such account it knows of; Siemens now points APE1808 operators to the available PAN-OS versions, and The Hacker News carries Unit 42's retraction.

alerts.summary: CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia", CVSS 7.8) is a local privilege escalation in the Linux kernel's xfrm ESP-in-TCP path, one of three CVEs Red Hat groups as "Dirty Frag"; CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, and Dream Research reports such a chain against 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and a US government-affiliated network. Its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache, and Red Hat confirms RHEL kernels are affected (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28 · Dream Research, 2026-10-29 · Red Hat RHSB-2026-003).

updates.summary: CVE-2026-46300's CVSS score has now been published (7.8) and Red Hat's own bulletin confirms RHEL kernels are affected (unlike sibling CVE-2026-43500, which Red Hat states does not affect its products). Public proof-of-concept exploits now target Kubernetes specifically, and Red Hat's bulletin groups this CVE under the collective "Dirty Frag" name alongside CVE-2026-43284/CVE-2026-43500, confirming the ESP-in-TCP exploitation path this entry already described and the coalescing-marker root cause are the same flaw.

The CVSS 7.8 figure came from the MITRE CVE record rather than from a cited advisory. It now cites Red Hat's CVE page, which publishes the same 7.8 score, and an evidence quote taken from the MITRE record is removed. The main text and action now carry the sourced interim mitigation (block esp4, esp6 and rxrpc, or disable unprivileged user namespaces) and the sourced patch status and discovery credits. Unsupported module names, a CAP_NET_ADMIN restriction, a kernel version range, wider patch coverage and a leftover table of three unrelated CVEs are removed, as is an unrelated actor link. The 2026-09-05 section now attributes the 7.8 score to Red Hat and cites Aikido for its container and detection guidance, which no longer says a module listing confirms IPsec use.

Aikido's statement that working Kubernetes proof-of-concept exploits have been published concerns the Dirty Frag family as a whole, not CVE-2026-46300 specifically; the summary and the 2026-09-05 section now attribute it that way, and no source describes a Kubernetes exploit for this CVE. Detection and triage lines are added from Wiz's description of the public exploit and Red Hat's list of legitimate user-namespace uses.

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root; Dream Research describes such a chain used against 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and a US government-affiliated network. The CVE record moves to exploited, the priority from notable to high, and the earlier statement that no source reports exploitation of this CVE is replaced. Removed from the text: the sentence that an attacker can modify any file the user can read (the Detection line still carries it) and, from the summary, the clause on Aikido's report of working Kubernetes exploits for the Dirty Frag family.

Dream Research's updated report names Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS as the product in the chain that paired the PHP2Shell flaws with this kernel flaw, and counts 25 rooted PAN-OS firewall and management servers; Unit 42 says it independently verified the tooling and results.

alerts.headline: Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: anonymous Super User flaws exploited since July; update to 2.20.4.2
alerts.summary: The mySites.guru research campaign against Joomla third-party extensions produced six further disclosures between 2026-07-20 and 2026-07-23, and one of them changes technique class: the Balbooa Gridbox page builder (CVE-2026-61425) trusts a client-supplied cookie value as proof of identity, so setting an administrator's username in that cookie authenticates the requester as that user with no password and no existing session. A Joomla Super User can edit templates, which is PHP execution, so this is full site compromise from a single anonymous request. Fixed in Gridbox 2.20.1; the researcher says the vulnerable code shipped for at least nine months. The same week added unauthenticated SQL injection and order-forgery flaws in EasyStore, an invoice IDOR in Events Booking, and a critical unauthenticated upload in Membership Pro. A follow-up audit of Gridbox produced eleven more CVEs, fixed in 2.20.2, four of them exploited in the wild, and Gridbox 2.20.3.1 (21 September) fixes a further unauthenticated SQL injection present in every earlier build. Gridbox 2.20.4.2 (27 October) fixes two more unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, with no exploitation reported.

updates.summary: A follow-on source-code audit of the Balbooa Gridbox page builder for Joomla, commissioned by the vendor after an earlier authentication-bypass disclosure, found 23 further vulnerabilities in the single component. Two now carry CVEs: CVE-2026-65884 (CVSS 4.0 10.0) because the registration handler adds the usergroup IDs a visitor asks for instead of replacing them, letting an anonymous user create an administrator account outright, and CVE-2026-65885 (CVSS 4.0 9.4), an authenticated arbitrary file upload that turns the first into end-to-end unauthenticated remote code execution. The Joomla CNA marks both as attacked, and the researcher reports server-log evidence of exploitation plus 92 planted administrator accounts on one connected site. Every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.1 is affected; the complete fix is Gridbox 2.20.2.

All eleven Joomla CNA records for the Gridbox 2.20.2 batch have now published. Seven are Critical, and four carry the exploit maturity Attacked: besides CVE-2026-65884 and CVE-2026-65885, already recorded here, CVE-2026-65887 resets the password of any account except Super Users and CVE-2026-65888 logs the caller in as any user through the social login method, both CVSS 4.0 10.0. Both are added. Balbooa has since shipped 2.20.2.3, a hardening release with no CVE, and 2.20.3.1, which fixes an unauthenticated blind SQL injection in the blog author parameter present in every earlier build, so the action now points at 2.20.3.1. The sourcing note reflects the exploitation now recorded and which parts rest on one source. The mySites.guru quotation follows the round-up's current text and names the page it comes from, and one phrase about how the coverage was produced is reworded. The summary mentions the follow-up releases, and verification is recorded as multi-source now that the vendor's release notes are among the sources.

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.

The analysis no longer says there is no exploitation signal or that the cookie name is withheld; the October 2025 release is treated as a lower bound on exposure, not its start; the CVE record's 9.4 score beside the discloser's 10.0, Membership Pro's CVSS 3.1 rating and its default-configuration impact, Balbooa's wording on web-server rules and the attribution of the read-side reading are corrected; the headline is current.

alerts.headline: PAN-OS management interfaces were rooted in the wild via PHP2Shell and a kernel flaw: hotfix, then check for compromise
alerts.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory, first published on 2026-10-21 and revised since, says active exploitation has been observed against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and Dream Research, with Unit 42's verification, reports a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw that rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea and went on to attack a US government-affiliated Active Directory. The advisory lists every release below the hotfix for its train, of PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 and of Panorama, as affected through the management web interface by CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS-B 9.2); all twenty hotfixes are released, and GlobalProtect and the captive portal are not affected. A device that was exposed and unpatched needs a compromise check as well as the hotfix, and CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.

updates.summary: Palo Alto Networks' revised advisory now also lists the WildFire appliances WF-500 and WF-500-B as affected by the PHP flaws in all versions, schedules hotfix builds of every PAN-OS train between 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-30, and leaves Panorama and WF-500 undated; Cortex XCORE (SaaS) and WildFire Cloud are already remediated.

Palo Alto Networks' advisory now lists the WildFire appliances WF-500 and WF-500-B as unaffected, a correction its timeline dates 2026-10-23, has no separate Panorama row while a note keeps Panorama in scope, and extends the Threat Prevention coverage; the PAN-OS hotfix dates of 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30 and the exploitation statement are unchanged.

Palo Alto's revision of 2026-10-25 lists the first three PAN-OS hotfixes (10.2.18-h13, 11.1.16-h4, 11.2.10-h16) as released, although its solution text still speaks of upcoming releases; the remaining hotfixes are due 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-30, and Palo Alto's current analysis finds no impact of CVE-2026-115560 on PAN-OS.
The entry said Unit 42 had seen a proof of concept of the PHP flaws; Unit 42's brief, revised on 2026-10-25, no longer says so, and the statement is removed.

Palo Alto Networks now records eleven PAN-OS hotfixes as released (10.2.13-h27, 10.2.16-h12, 10.2.18-h13, 11.1.4-h38, 11.1.6-h40, 11.1.10-h36, 11.1.13-h16, 11.1.16-h4, 11.2.10-h16, 12.1.7-h11 and 12.2.4-h1) with nine others due by 2026-10-30; CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, while Palo Alto still reports no malicious exploitation against its products.

Dream Research's report, updated 2026-10-29, names Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS as the product behind the chain it had first described with an unnamed vendor: a custom PHP2Shell build chained with a Linux kernel flaw rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers and was followed by an attack on a US government-affiliated Active Directory, and Unit 42 says it independently verified the tooling and results. The advisory's exploitation statement is unchanged; a device that was exposed and unpatched needs a compromise check as well as the hotfix, and Dream says the affected web server also fronts the GlobalProtect portal, which Palo Alto's advisory lists as not affected.
